subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this trusted-source taxonomy, repurpose the existing `--force` flag as provenance acknowledgement for arbitrary first installs, and make Crestodian trusted-source-only?
rationale: The code and proof support the proposed behavior, but automation cannot decide whether breaking unattended install commands and removing arbitrary Crestodian installs is the intended permanent product and security contract.

options.title: Approve The Boundary
options.body: Accept the compatibility changes and land after required checks pass, with release communication explaining the new noninteractive and Crestodian behavior.

options.title: Use A Separate Ack Flag
options.body: Preserve `--force` as overwrite-only and add a distinct acknowledgement flag, reducing semantic overload at the cost of another public CLI option.

options.title: Keep Crestodian Approval
options.body: Allow arbitrary Crestodian sources only through a stronger typed approval flow instead of requiring a trusted shell, which broadens this PR's security design.

recommendation.title: Approve The Boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the compatibility changes and land after required checks pass, with release communication explaining the new noninteractive and Crestodian behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is on the central plugin installer and manifest paths that define this boundary.
